items.title: 체코 원전 순항…한수원, 냉각탑 입찰 설명회 성료

items.title: 앤트로픽·AMD發 악재 겹친 코스피…4%대 급락 지속

items.title: 李대통령 "주가조작·시세조종 뿌리 뽑겠다…부당이득 철저 환수"

items.title: 메리츠증권, 정책·기관 출자 사업 '6전 6패'…미래벤처와 '마수걸이' 도전

items.title: 카카오 김범수 SM엔터 시세조종 혐의 2심 무죄(종합)
items.snippet: 김범수 카카오 미래이니셔티브센터장이 SM엔터테인먼트 주가 시세조종 혐의와 관련해 2심에서 무죄를 선고받았다.재판부는 카카오의 대규모 주식 매수가 시장가격에 영향을 미쳤더라도 이를 시세조종으로 단정할 수 없다고 판단했다.서울고법 형사4-1부(김인경 성지용 전지원 부장판사)는 20일 서초구 고등법원에서 열린 2심에서 재판부는 무죄를 선고받은 1심의 판단을 그대로 유지한다며 검찰의 항소를 기각했다.함께 기소된 배재현 전 카카오 투자총괄대표도 1심과 같이 무죄를 선고받았다.김 센터장 등은 2023년 2월 하이브[352820]의 SM엔터테

items.title: 남매 계열분리 청구서 받은 신세계…단기차입 6천억 늘었다
items.snippet: 신세계그룹 남매의 결별 비용이 신세계의 재무제표에도 반영됐다. items.title: 메모리는 HBM 개발통, 갤럭시는 퀄컴 출신…삼성전자 투톱 겸직 해제

items.title: 신한증권·벤처, LP 성장펀드 펀드레이징 나섰다

items.title: 앤트로픽 상장 여파에 유동성 이탈…코스피 4% 급락 출발(상보)

items.title: 제지업계, 인쇄용지 가격 연내 인상 추진
items.snippet: 주요 제지업체들이 인쇄용지 가격을 조만간 잇따라 인상할 전망이다. 원재료 가격 인상과 물류비 상승 등으로 수익성이 점점 더 악화하는 데 따른 것이다. 19일 제지업계에 따르면 한솔제지는 다음달 초 일반지 가격을 13%, 모조지 가격을 10% 인상하겠다는 방침을 최근 거래처들에 통보했다. 무림페이퍼도 연내에 인쇄용지 가격을 인상하는 방안을 검토 중인 것으로 알려졌다. 인쇄용지 점유율 1·2위인 한솔제지와 무림페이퍼는 지난 3분기에 나란히 적자를 기록했다. 펄프 등 원자재 가격이 오른데다 물류비 상승, 환율 하락까지 겹친 영향이다.

items.snippet: 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 아시아 순방을 계기로 김정은 북한 국무위원장과의 만남을 타진했지만 김 위원장이 호응하지 않으면서 2019년 이후 7년 만에 개최 가능성이 제기된 북-미 정상회담은 지난해 경주 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의에 이어 재차 무산됐다. APEC 정상회의 참석차 중국 선전을 찾은 트럼프 대통령이 19일(현지 시간) 출국한 날 김 위원장은 북-중 접경에서 떨어진 함경남도 시찰 행보를 공개하며 미국을 향해 ‘내치’에 집중하고 있다는 메시지를 냈다.● 트럼프 회동 제안에 보란 듯 시찰 공개한 김정은김 위원장은 18일 함경남도 함흥시에 있는 김정숙해군대학을 방문해 현지지도에 나섰다고 19일 조선중앙통신이 밝혔다. 통신은 17, 18일엔 함경남도 리원군과 락원군의 지방발전정책 대상 건설장을 방문했다고 전했다. 이에 앞서...

items.title: 李, 푸틴과 첫 대면… 靑 “북핵문제 논의”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 중국 선전에서 열린 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의 기간 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령, 시진핑(習近平) 중국 국가주석, 블라디미르 푸틴 러시아 대통령과 잇따라 만나 정상외교에 나섰다. 청와대에 따르면 이 대통령은 18일 시 주석 주최로 열린 APEC 정상회의 환영 만찬에서 푸틴 대통령과 만나 약 10분간 회동을 갖고 북핵을 비롯한 한반도 문제를 논의했다. 한국 대통령이 러시아 정상과 만난 것은 2019년 문재인 전 대통령 이후 7년 만이다. 청와대 고위 관계자는 기자들과 만나 “(한-러 관계가) 여러 여건상 쉽지 않지만 문제가 없는 영역에서 협력 여지를 찾아 관계를 잘 관리해 나가자는 데 대체적인 의견의 일치가 있었다”며 “북한 핵 문제도 다루어졌다”고 말했다. 청와대는 같은 날 열린 이 대통령과 시 주석의 35분간 정...

items.title: 박찬종 前의원 별세… 고인 뜻대로 시신 기증, 조문 안받아
items.snippet: 5선 국회의원을 지낸 박찬종 변호사(사진)가 18일 별세했다. 향년 87세. 19일 유족에 따르면 고인은 전날 오후 숙환으로 별세했다. 고인의 뜻에 따라 유족은 조문을 받지 않은 채 가족장으로 장례를 마쳤고, 시신은 서울 세브란스병원에 기증했다. 고인은 1992년 시신 기증 약속을 한 것으로 알려졌다. 경남 김해 출신인 고인은 경기고와 서울대 경제학과를 졸업하고 고등고시 사법과와 행정과에 합격해 검사로 공직 생활을 시작했다. 1973년 9대 총선에서 당시 여당인 민주공화당 소속으로 부산에서 당선되며 정계에 입문해 5선 의원을 지냈다. 고인은 김영삼 김대중 김종필 등 ‘3김’의 뒤를 이을 차세대 정치인으로 주목받았다. 1992년 14대 대선 국면에서 한때 지지율 1위를 달렸고, 151만6047표(6.37%)를 득표하며 최종 4위를 기록했다. 1...

items.title: 두달간 수능 부정행위 신고 접수… 최대 1억 포상
items.snippet: 정부가 2027학년도 대학수학능력시험(수능)이 끝난 바로 다음 날부터 ‘범정부 태스크포스(TF)’를 가동해 인공지능(AI) 등 첨단 기기를 활용한 부정행위에 대한 즉각적인 조사에 나선다. 부정행위자에 대한 신고 포상금도 최대 1억 원까지 지급할 예정이다. 19일 관계부처에 따르면 수능 다음 날인 20일부터 한성숙 국무총리를 반장으로 한 ‘범정부 수능 부정행위 TF’가 가동된다. 수능 종료 후에도 제기되는 부정행위를 예외 없이 적발하기 위해서다. 교육부 장관이 TF 간사를 맡고 과학기술 부총리, 법무부·행정안전부 장관, 경찰청장 등이 참여한다. TF는 글로벌 빅테크 기업과 통신사와 협력해 부정행위 의심 사례를 조사하고 신고나 제보, 민원 등을 다각도로 검토해 수능 부정행위자를 적발할 방침이다. 특히 권익위원회는 20일부터 내년 1월 19일까지...

items.title: “재건축 이익 과도하게 산정” 조합들 줄소송-집회 예고
items.snippet: 국토교통부가 재건축초과이익환수제(재초환)에 따른 부담금 부과 시한을 연장할 수 없다고 밝히자 재건축조합들은 소송과 집회를 예고했다. 당장 연내 부과를 앞둔 서울 서초구 반포현대(현 반포센트레빌아스테리움) 재건축조합은 소송에 나설 방침이고, 전국 재건축조합들은 다음 달 청와대 앞에서 제도 폐지를 촉구하기로 했다. 정치권에서도 재건축 위축으로 주택 공급이 줄어들 수 있다는 비판이 나왔다. 서울 서초구 반포현대 재건축 조합은 19일 동아일보와의 통화에서 “12월 부담금이 부과되는 대로 법적 대응에 나서겠다”고 밝혔다. 조합이 특히 문제 삼는 건 정상주택가격상승분이다. 재건축을 하지 않았어도 올랐을 것으로 보고 부담금 산정 때 빼주는 금액이다. 조합 측은 “재건축을 하지 않은 인근 아파트도 집값이 비슷하게 올랐다”며 “정상주택가격상승분을 지나치게 낮...

items.title: [단독]국세청장 후보자, 아내 명의로 재개발 주택 매입후 비거주
items.snippet: 안덕수 국세청장 후보자(사진)가 2010년부터 서울 뉴타운 지역 주택을 배우자 명의로 보유하며 신축 아파트를 취득했지만 실거주하지 않은 것으로 나타났다. 19일 국회에 제출된 인사청문요청안 등에 따르면 안 후보자는 배우자가 서울 동대문구 이문동 래미안라그란데 1채(74㎡)를 보유하고 있다고 신고했다. 2006년 재정비촉진구역(뉴타운)으로 지정된 이문1구역을 3069채로 재개발한 이 아파트는 지난해 1월 완공됐다. 안 후보자의 아내는 2010년 5월 이 주택을 매입했지만 안 후보자 가족은 실거주하지 않았고, 2018년 철거와 이주가 시작돼 지난해 1월 완공된 후에는 전세를 준 것으로 나타났다. 74㎡의 경우 세대 분리형으로 설계돼 2명의 임차인에게 4억5000만 원, 1억8000만 원에 각각 전세를 준 것으로 파악됐다. 2010년 매입 이후 실...

items.title: 李, 순방중 조작기소 특검법 의결 당일 재가… 野 “기습 재가” 반발
items.snippet: 윤석열 정부 시절 이재명 대통령 등에 대한 검찰의 조작수사 및 기소 의혹을 규명하기 위한 조작기소 특검법이 해외 순방 중인 이 대통령의 재가를 거쳐 19일 공포됐다. 국민의힘은 “‘대리 의결’에 이어 해외 순방 중에 ‘이재명 탈옥법’을 ‘기습 재가’했다”고 반발했다. 정부는 이날 ‘윤석열 정권 검찰청·국가정보원·감사원 등의 조작수사·조작기소 등 의혹의 진상 규명을 위한 특별검사 임명 등에 관한 법률’을 관보에 게재해 공포했다. 법은 공포 즉시 시행된다. 이재명 정부 출범 후 7번째 특검으로 특검팀은 최대 309명 규모이고 수사 기간은 준비 기간을 포함해 최장 200일이다. 윤석열 정부 시절 이뤄진 총 17건의 수사에서 검찰의 권한 남용이 있었는지가 특검 수사 대상인데 이 중 ‘쌍방울 불법 대북송금 의혹’, ‘대장동 개발사업 특혜 의혹’ 등 8...

items.title: 與 ‘민주유공자법’ 본회의 상정… 국힘 필버로 맞서

items.title: 김건희 ‘도이치-통일교’ 징역 4년 확정… 명태균 여론조사 무죄
items.snippet: 대법원이 도이치모터스 주가조작, 통일교 금품 수수 등 이른바 ‘3대 의혹’으로 재판에 넘겨진 윤석열 전 대통령의 부인 김건희 여사에게 징역 4년을 확정했다. 주가조작 가담과 통일교 금품 수수 혐의는 유죄로, 명태균 씨의 여론조사 무상 수수 혐의는 무죄로 판단했다. 영부인 출신이 형사 범죄로 실형을 확정받은 것은 헌정사상 처음이다. 19일 대법원 전원합의체(주심 박영재 대법관)는 “자본시장법 위반 등에 관한 원심 판단에 잘못이 없다”며 김 여사에게 징역 4년에 벌금 5000만 원을 선고한 원심을 확정했다. 도이치모터스 주가조작 및 통일교 금품 수수 혐의에 대해선 대법관 전원이 유죄로 판단했다. ‘명태균 무상 여론조사 제공’ 혐의는 10 대 2 의견으로 무죄가 확정됐다. 오경미, 김성수 대법관은 유죄 취지로 파기 환송해야 한다는 반대의견을 남겼다...

items.title: 연봉 2억 여행사 지사장, 노가리 끊고 비건 박람회 연 사연
items.snippet: 2016년 인도네시아 발리. 김종훈(56)씨는 길리섬에 가는 쾌속정에 올라탔다. 길리섬은 발리 동쪽 롬복섬 인근에 있는 유명 휴양지. 배는 시속 50㎞로 파도를 갈랐다. 선장이 갑자기 배를 왼쪽으로 크게 틀었다. 김씨는 하마터면 바다에 빠질 뻔했다. 오른쪽에는 거대한 쓰레기 더미가 둥둥 떠 있었다. 선장 옆 직원이 “TRASH(쓰레기)!”를 외칠 때마다 배가 요동쳤다. 승객들은 의자를 움켜쥐었고, 이런 일이 30분간 반복되자 모두 멀미를 했다. 길리섬의 스노클링 명소로 꼽히는 바다도 마찬가지였다. 플라스틱병과 비닐봉지, 스티로폼 박스가 떠 있었다. 가이드는 물속은 아름다우니 뛰어들라고 권했다. 수영복을 입은 외국인 관광객들은 멋쩍게 웃기만 했다. 아무도 물에 들어가지 않았다. 한 외국인은 “해변이라기보단 쓰레기장에 가깝다”고 했다.

items.snippet: 19일 치러진 2027학년도 대학수학능력시험(수능)은 어려웠던 작년 수능보다 쉽게 출제된 것으로 분석된다. 국어와 영어 영역은 작년보다 쉬웠고 수학은 지난해와 비슷하게 변별력을 유지한 것으로 분석된다. 입시 전문가들은 상위권 변별력이 수학 영역에서 확보될 것으로 평가했다.

items.title: EU moves towards 10-year probation period for new members - starting with Montenegro
items.snippet: EU ambassadors broadly backed a 10-year probation period for newcomers, with voting rights open to suspension for Orbán-style breaches, as a basis for Montenegro’s treaty.

items.title: 서울역서 강남 25분… 27일부터 심야 급행 좌석버스 달린다
items.snippet: 서울 도심 주요 지역을 연결하는 심야 좌석버스가 운행을 시작한다. 서울시는 오는 27일부터 심야 좌석버스 ‘반딧불이버스’를 운행한다고 19일 밝혔다. 홍대입구역과 신촌역, 광화문역, 을지로입구역, 동대문디자인플라자(DDP), 명동역, 서울역, 고속터미널역, 논현역, 강남역 등을 연결한다.

items.title: 344억 들였는데 “쓰레기통”… 창원 빅트리, 전망대 탈바꿈
items.snippet: 조감도와 너무 달라 “통나무 쓰레기통 같다”는 비판을 받은 경남 창원 전망대 ‘빅트리(Big Tree)’가 리모델링된다. 창원시는 55억원을 추가로 들여 빅트리 꼭대기에 실내 전망대와 카페를 짓기로 했다고 19일 밝혔다.

items.title: 금천구청, 광주역, 구포~가야… 48조 들여 전국 9곳 지상 철도 지하화
items.snippet: 서울 도심을 가로지르는 수도권 전철 1호선의 주요 지상 철도 구간이 지하화된다. 정부는 19일 경부선(서울역~금천구청역·34.7㎞)과 경원선(서빙고역~도봉산역·32.9㎞), 경인선(온수역~인천역·22.8㎞) 등 전국 철도 구간 9곳(총 112.1㎞)에 대한 ‘철도 지하화 사업’을 새로 추진한다고 밝혔다. 철도를 지하로 옮긴 뒤 확보한 지상 구간에는 주거·상업 시설과 공원 등이 조성된다. 이는 총 48조5000억원이 투입되는 대규모 신규 사업(기존 지하화 사업 3곳 포함 시 53조6000억원)이다. 하지만 철도 부지 개발 이익만으로 충당할 수 없는 사업비가 11조1000억원에 이르는데다, 정부가 이를 지방자치단체에 부담시킬 방침이어서 난관도 예상된다.

items.title: 추미애, 김동연표 현금성 복지 대폭 축소·폐지 나서
items.snippet: 김동연 전 경기지사가 역점 추진했던 ‘기회소득’ 사업이 시행 3~4년 만에 대폭 축소될 전망이다. ‘재정 비상’을 선언한 경기도가 정책 효과가 불명확하다는 이유로 내년도 예산안에서 6개 사업 중 4개 사업 예산을 뺐기 때문이다. 나머지 장애인 기회소득 예산은 올해보다 55.5%, 농어민 기회소득은 18.6% 줄였다. 도의회가 예산안을 그대로 확정하면 6개 사업 예산은 올해 995억원에서 내년 428억원으로 57% 줄어든다.

items.title: 제32회 장한 고대언론인상
items.snippet: 고려대 언론인교우회(회장 곽영길)는 19일 제32회 ‘장한 고대언론인상’ 수상자를 발표했다. 신성식 중앙일보 보건복지전문기자, 신석호 동아닷컴 대표, 황준범 한겨레 편집국장, 이주희 코리아헤럴드 편집국장이 본상 수상자로 선정됐고, 금교돈 전 조선교육문화미디어 대표가 공로상 수상자로 선정됐다. 시상식은 12월 2일 고려대 수당삼양패컬티하우스에서 열릴 예정이다.

items.snippet: 온 가족에게 기쁨을 안겨 준 아기의 탄생을 알려주세요. 홈페이지 주소 입력창에 아가야안녕.com이라고 입력하면 됩니다. 매일유업 육아 정보 사이트 매일아이(maeili.com)를 통해서도 접속할 수 있습니다. 추첨을 통해 출산 소식과 사진이 지면에 실린 가족에게는 ①케이크 구매권 ②엄마와 아이를 위한 매일두 포인트 3만원 ③출산 소식을 생일 날짜 본지 1면에 담은 PDF 파일 ④조선일보 1개월 무료 구독권을 드립니다. 당첨자 중 한 가족을 선정하여 해당 지면을 고급 프레임에 담아 제공하는 조선일보 리프린트도 제작해 드립니다. 홈페이지에서는 균형 영양식 메디웰 2만원 할인 혜택도 드리고 있습니다.

items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

items.title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
items.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establ...

items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. With Claude Opus 5.5, C...

items.snippet: 국제원자력기구(IAEA)가 19일 한국의 핵추진잠수함(핵잠) 도입에 필요한 한국의 핵 비확산 및 안전조치 의무 이행에 대해 “만족한다(satisfied)”고 평가한 보고서를 발간했다. 국제사회에서 한국의 핵잠 도입이 핵 확산이 아니라 평화적 활동이라는 점을 인정받기 위한 첫 발을 내디딘 것으로 풀이된다. 다만 한국보다 먼저 핵잠 보유를 선언한 호주와 브라질도 IAEA와 수년씩 협의를 이어오고 있어 한국도 상당한 시간이 소요될 수 있다는 관측이 나온다. IAEA는 이날 한국의 핵잠사업 추진 경과와 한국 정부와의 협의 내용, 안전조치 의무이행 현황 등을 담은 보고서를 공개했다. IAEA는 2022년부터는 호주에 대해, 2023년부터는 브라질과 연례 보고서를 발간하고 있으며 한국에 대해서는 처음으로 라파엘 그로시 사무총장 명의의 보고서를 발간했다....

items.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. items.abstract: Advanced technology nodes improve performance but increase susceptibility to BTI-induced aging. Using aging- aware circuit simulations, we show that realistic on-chip thermal gradients can cause significant asymmetric transistor degradation in 16 nm FinFET circuits, leading to setup and hold time violations. items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{max} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{br}I_{max}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Atomic-scale assembly of sulfur vacancy complexes for tailored in-gap states in monolayer WS$_{2}$
items.abstract: Atomic-scale defects in two-dimensional semiconductors are quasi-isolated quantum systems with promise for emerging technologies. Although their potential as spin qubits, quantum sensors and single-photon emitters has been demonstrated experimentally, creating them deterministically and identifying them chemically remains challenging, which limits control over their electronic states. In this work we assemble sulfur vacancies in monolayer WS$_{2}$ into complexes of different sizes and geometries using the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope. We study their electronic properties by a combination of scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory, revealing the intricate influences of geometry, underlying point group symmetries and spin-orbit coupling on hybridized states. items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

items.title: Delay Mismatches Shape the Spectra of Three Synchronized Semiconductor Lasers
items.abstract: We study a network of three synchronized chaotic lasers and the radio frequency spectra of the intensity fluctuations. The position and morphology of the peaks are significantly different depending on the set of lasers being synchronized. The lasers and coupling paths are similar but not identical in all parameters, including their feedback and coupling delay times. The inverse of the delay mismatch between each pair of lasers introduces characteristic frequencies that shape the spectral response of the synchronized system. By studying two different three-laser configurations, we find that peaks appear whenever multiple harmonic contributions overlap in frequency, resulting in constructive enhancement of the spectral power. items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. items.title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. items.title: A Probabilistic Behavioral RTL Simulation Framework for Probabilistic Compute Fabrics
items.abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. items.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
items.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. items.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
items.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-or...

items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.abstract: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. items.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
items.abstract: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. items.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU
items.abstract: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. items.abstract: Topological insulator field-effect transistors (TIFETs) have emerged as a promising alternative to overcome the scaling limits of silicon-based field-effect transistors (Si-based FETs). items.abstract: The generation and control of circularly polarized and chiral light is important for a wide range of applications, from sensing to optical communication and catalysis. We exploit the $π$/2 phase difference between the transverse and longitudinal components of the electric field that is carried by 30 keV electrons, to coherently excite degenerate dipolar modes of which the far-field radiation interferes in the far field, thereby creating a strong optical spin-Hall effect. items.title: Koopmans spectral functionals for excitons in materials
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles characterization of excitons typically relies on the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) combined with quasiparticle energies from computationally demanding GW calculations. Here, we replace the GW step with quasiparticle energies from Koopmans-compliant spectral functionals, an approach we call BSE@qKI, and implement it in an automated, reproducible AiiDA workflow. For a set of benchmark semiconductors, BSE@qKI reproduces experimental band gaps and first exciton energies with mean absolute relative errors of 13% and 4%, respectively, comparable to BSE@G0W0 for the gaps and markedly better for the excitation energies. We also apply the method to the layered magnetic semiconductor CrI3, obtaining an absorption spectrum that reproduces the main experimental features. These results establish BSE@qKI as a GW-free alternative to BSE@G0W0 for systematic studies of excitonic...

items.title: A Discrete Digital Isolator with Shielded Planar Transformer for Gate Driver Applications
items.abstract: Galvanically isolated gate drivers are required in many power electronics applications. This paper describes an implementation of a digital isolator using discrete components with a planar coreless PCB signal transformer providing the isolation. The use of an electrostatic shield between the transformer windings is shown to provide sufficient common-mode transient immunity to support IGBT half-bridge drivers, an application subject to a severe dV/dt transient during switching. The design is verified through the experimental implementation of a prototype half bridge using two of the proposed discrete digital isolators with SiC power transistors and demonstrates common-mode transient immunity greater than 15 kV/us with very low implementation complexity.

items.title: Reconfigurable 2D Lateral Heterostructure Platform for Unified Detection, Emission, and Logic
items.abstract: Heterogeneous integration of sensing, light generation, communication, and computation typically requires specialized devices, resulting in complex interconnects, fabrication overhead, parasitic losses, and energy penalties. Developing a monolithic, reconfigurable device capable of controlling carrier generation, transport, and recombination remains a longstanding challenge. Two-dimensional (2D) lateral heterostructures offer a promising approach by combining spatially distinct domains of different charge polarity with a dynamically tunable electrostatic landscape. Here, multifunctional bilayer MoSe2-WSe2 lateral heterojunctions are demonstrated, integrating photodetection, reconfigurable electroluminescence (EL), and CMOS logic operation within a unified platform. items.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
items.abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. items.abstract: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody. We analyze a 3D box with such mirrors as walls to accumulate and store blackbody radiation. Applications include solar-powered thermal energy and solar-powered thermophotovoltaics. items.abstract: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. items.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
items.abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed...

items.title: A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation
items.abstract: Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. items.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $Γ$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. items.title: Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
items.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. items.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
items.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. items.title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
items.abstract: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. items.title: DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration
items.abstract: Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. items.title: Porosification of the dielectric layer in alternating-current electroluminescence devices enables high-resolution tactile imaging
items.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. We identify a nonlinear capacitance-dependent emission window that provides a basis for tunable pressure-to-light conversion. Pore-size engineering further suppresses local emission deficiencies, reducing spatial intensity variation by nearly ninefold and enabling faithful imaging of contact features down to 100 μm. items.abstract: This work highlights the potential of combining event-based signaling with event-driven reception to achieve receiver power scaling across link utilization, without requiring wake-up, locking, or data-rate reconfiguration. The approach is demonstrated using the proposed four-level Gaussian pulse-amplitude modulation (GPAM-4) scheme and a corresponding event-driven receiver. items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnet...

items.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
items.abstract: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. Nominal results include 41.711 microwatts biased neuron-core power, 3.338-pJ positive terminal energy for a 1.4-microsecond cell read, and 0.531-mV selected-state drift over a 5-ms extracted-tile hold...

items.title: Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass
items.abstract: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors offer distinct advantages as imaging detectors for space-based X-ray observatories, being low-power, radiation-resistant, and operable at room temperature. Previous characterizations of the low-cost, commercially-available IMX290LLR-C back-illuminated CMOS sensor from Sony Semiconductor Solutions have found Fano-limited X-ray spectral resolutions while operated at room temperature and a radiation tolerance compatible with use in low Earth orbit. Here, we report the quantum efficiency of the IMX290LLR-C as measured across the soft X-ray band (200 - 1000 eV) using Beamline 6.3.2 of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. We find a quantum efficiency of roughly 10 -- 40\% over this band, and fit these measurements to a quantum efficiency model constrained by these measurements and microscopy of the sens...

items.title: Characterization of the GIGAPYX-4600 CMOS visible image sensor in the context of high precision astrometry
items.abstract: To evaluate the potential of detectors for next-generation space astrometry missions such as the HWO and Theia, an extensive analysis of the performance of the GIGAPYX-4600 46-megapixel CMOS detector from Pyxalis was conducted at IPAG. The 5456x8320-pixel detector, featuring a 4.4-micron pitch and back-side illumination, constitutes a matrix of 24x36 mm. It has a measured gain of 13.3 electrons per ADU in low-gain mode. The saturation level of the detector in low-gain-mode is estimated to be approximately 52 000 electrons. This sensor demonstrates linearity errors of 0.90%, pixel response non-uniformity of less than 1.3%, and readout and quantization noise of 12 electrons in low-gain mode. Dark current was measured at 35 electrons per second at 35{\textdegree}C and inter-pixel capacitance remained under 3%. We demonstrated that inter-pixel capacitance effects can be effectively mitigated...

items.title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
items.abstract: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. CGTransformer achieves high generation validity and the highest single shot crystal structure prediction (CSP) match rate among the compar...

items.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
items.abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. The interlayer charge transfer shows strong spin selectivity and is governed by the relative alignment between the valley-spin polari...

items.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
items.abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. We analyze their structural motifs, stability, and electronic band structures, highlighting recurring prototype families, several of which show intrinsic intermediate-band features. Our res...

items.title: CHARMING: Parallel Edge AI Acceleration Across Tensor Processing and In-Memory Computation
items.abstract: Edge AI increasingly relies on specialized accelerators for low-latency inference under tight resource and energy constraints, yet their efficiency remains limited by data movement. Prior work, CHARM, mitigates this overhead by overlapping data movement with computation. We observe that in-memory computing can further supplement tensor processing as a parallel accelerator while eliminating certain data movements entirely. We present CHARMING, a heterogeneous edge AI architecture that uses accuracy- and quantization-aware partitioning to distribute and concurrently execute inference workloads across tensor processing and in-memory computation. CHARMING partitions attention heads between an AIE array and an in-DRAM compute unit, balancing execution according to model architecture, sequence length, and precision while selecting heads to minimize accuracy degradation. CHARMING also integrate...

items.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
items.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering...

items.title: SPLIT-MOR: Fast and Accurate Model Order Reduction for Nonlinear Transient Thermal Simulation of 2.5D/3D ICs
items.abstract: Fast and accurate transient thermal simulation is essential to thermal reliability analysis and dynamic thermal management of advanced packages, and model order reduction (MOR) techniques are widely applied to overcome the efficiency bottleneck of rigorous numerical methods. However, nonlinear terms including temperature-dependent leakage power, thermal conductivity, and heat capacity prevent the application of conventional linear MOR, while hyper-reduction solutions require costly nonlinear training data. In this work, we propose SPLIT-MOR (Subdomain-wise Piecewise Linearization with Interval Tensors), a novel nonlinear MOR method that requires no additional training set. SPLIT-MOR computes reduced component tensors by subdomain clustering and temperature-interval partitioning in the offline stage, and updates the reduced coefficient matrices and load vectors efficiently in the online s...

items.title: Contrastive local learning in large nonlinear analog circuits
items.abstract: Machine learning in physical hardware promises to reduce training cost by colocating computation, memory and adaptation within device physics. Contrastive local learning networks (CLLNs) offer a compelling route: an electrical circuit relaxes to equilibrium in free and weakly clamped states, and each adaptive element updates from local voltage contrasts rather than backpropagated error signals. Yet whether nonlinear transistor implementations can scale beyond proof-of-concept circuits, and what design principles control that scaling, have remained unknown. Here we show that nonlinear analog circuits trained by contrastive local rules can learn larger machine-learning tasks and remain robust under hardware nonidealities. Using device-level circuit simulations, we systematically explore initialization, operating regime, loss-dependent clamping and training parameters, and scale CLLNs beyon...

items.title: Composition Driven Band Alignment Evolution in Grafted Si/GeSn Heterostructures
items.abstract: Understanding and controlling band alignment in lattice-mismatched group-IV semiconductor-based heterostructures is fundamental to rational band-structure engineering, as it governs the electronic structure and carrier transport in heterointegrated semiconductor systems. Despite growing interest in Si/GeSn heterostructures, the composition-dependent band alignment has not been experimentally established. Here, we experimentally establish the evolution of band alignment in semiconductor-grafted Si/GeSn heterostructures with contents ranging from 8.8% to 12.4% using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Kraut's core-level method. The valence-band offset increases systematically from ~0.29 to ~0.57 eV with increasing Sn composition, whereas the corresponding effective conduction-band offset decreases from ~0.30 to ~0.12 eV. The observed band-alignment evolution is attributed to an upward shi...

items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
items.abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. Across 13 model--harness configurations, 91.1\% of attempts produce GDS layouts, but only 23.0\% satisfy the benchmark's acceptance criteria. We also evaluate Novara, a...

items.title: Interfacial Effects of Thermal Reorganization on Charge and Spin Transport in Organic Spin Valves
items.abstract: Organic semiconductors are attractive for spintronic applications owing to their weak spin-orbit coupling, small hyperfine interactions, mechanical flexibility, and tunable electronic properties. Organic spin valves (OSVs) provide a representative platform for investigating spin-dependent transport. However, the magnetoresistance (MR) response is highly sensitive to the ferromagnetic electrode/organic semiconductor interface (spinterface). Variations in interfacial morphology, chemical interaction, energy-level alignment, and spin polarization can strongly affect spin injection, transport, and detection, making reproducible OSV performance difficult to achieve. Here, we investigate how in situ thermal annealing affects the electrical and magnetotransport properties of complete NDI-based OSVs. items.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
items.abstract: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy demonstrates electrostatic tuning of the qubit transition over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference show coherent qubit control, with representative values T1 = 0.79 us and T2* = 0.91 us. Across five gatemons distributed over three chips, the measured relaxation times range from approximately 0.2 us to 1 us and decrease with increasing qubit frequency. Their magnitude is comparable to a circuit estimate of spontaneous emission into the electromagnetic environment. These results establish in-s...

items.title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
items.abstract: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. items.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array. Furthermore, we apply these devices to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR),...

items.title: High-Quality InSb Nanowires Grown by Molecular-Beam Epitaxy via Precise Catalyst Modulation
items.abstract: Semiconductor InSb nanowires are a major material candidate for topological quantum computation. The nanowires in current devices were mostly grown using metal organic chemical vapor deposition, incompatible with in situ growth of superconductor, a crucial requirement for low-disorder devices. Growth of InSb nanowires using molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) can address this issue. So far, studies on MBE-grown InSb remain limited due to an extremely narrow parameter window for the growth and reproducibility. Moreover, the use of foreign catalysts can introduce deep-level impurities. Here, we report a self-catalyzed MBE growth of InSb nanowires without those foreign catalysts. We first grow GaAs nanowire stems, and then convert Ga catalyst droplets into In droplets in situ. Axial heteroepitaxial growth of InSb can be realized through the In droplets on top of GaAs stems. items.title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
items.abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. The framework is evaluated against a feature-engineered supervised baseline under three conditions: limited label...

Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
items.abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. Additionally, we propose a novel concept for an all-optical isolator based on spin...

items.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function
items.abstract: By utilizing the derivation of quantum Cramér-Rao bound and an argument put forward by Efimov and Dodonov, we derive several uncertainty relations for mixed states that constrain the diagonal product, trace, and each diagonal element of the covariance matrix of multiple observables. By choosing the observables to be the symmetric logarithmic derivative, the uncertainty relations imply various geometric bounds on quantum Fisher information matrix caused by mean Uhlmann curvature, which in pure states become geometric bounds on quantum metric caused by Berry curvature. Our formalism reveals optical sum rules for velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and how they are bounded by the Berry curvature and commutator of velocity operators. items.title: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE
items.abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junctions with crystalline tunnel barriers have remained elusive by epitaxial techniques such as MOCVD or MBE that produce the junction materials and devices powering today's electronic and photonic systems like transistors and lasers. Here, we overcome the key materials hurdle to realize the first functional nitride crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE. Despite an AlN barrier thickness of approximately 4.5 nm, the NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers exhibit coherent Josephson tunneling with critical current densities of approximately 17 A/cm2, an IcRn product of approximately 2.5 mV, and a superconducting gap voltage of approximately 3.7 mV with a BCS-like gap evolution with temperature. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-tran...

items.title: Adjoint-State Identifiability of Piezo-Tunable Valley Splitting in 2D Magnetic Heterostructures
items.abstract: Mechanical strain has been proposed to dynamically tune proximity-induced valley splitting in 2D magnetic heterostructures for solid-state information processing. While first-principles studies routinely predict strain-modulated valley splittings at the atomic scale, they rarely address whether the coupling parameter can be extracted from a macroscopic transport measurement against realistic device noise. This paper develops a classical, partial differential equation-constrained multiscale inverse framework to quantify the device-level identifiability of the exchange-strain coupling from a transverse Hall voltage in a molybdenum disulfide and chromium tribromide heterostructure. Structural relaxation confirms a chiral $C_3$ point-group symmetry of the Hollow-stacked structure, and Neumann's principle reduces the coupling tensor to a single scalar $η$. items.title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs
items.abstract: New AI accelerators arrive before the kernels that make them fast, because peak kernel performance requires architecture-specific expertise in operand pipelines and data-movement techniques. Coding agents can now write, compile, and tune kernels on their own, so they could greatly accelerate kernel development and optimization. What agents produce depends on the interfaces they are given. These interfaces may expose a machine's raw capabilities or encode the known-good methods for exploiting its hardware features efficiently. We test the performance impact of these two interfaces on Intel GPUs through controlled experiments with five coding models on three kernels. With raw SYCL and execution feedback, Opus 4.8, the strongest of the three models tested with Claude Code, writes a single-GPU GEMM kernel reaching only 57.5% of Intel's tuned oneDNN library. We present SyclKittens, a hardware...

items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These pri...

items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. We therefore introduce Splash, an architecture that virtualizes HBM and HBF for the KV cache. We architect custom HBM and HBF base dies with novel memory and flash cont...

items.title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning
items.abstract: High-throughput calculations using density-functional theory (DFT) are commonly used to explore point defects for applications in power electronics and quantum technologies. There is currently a major shift away from these traditional simulation techniques towards machine learning (ML) methods. We explore a class of physics-guided ML models for predicting defect formation energies and zero-phonon lines (ZPL) to identify point defects for quantum applications. The models are specifically targeted for use in a prescreening step for accelerated high-throughput workflows, and are therefore designed to avoid the costly relaxation step typically present with ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We compare performance for single and double point defect systems in 4H-SiC with ridge, kernel ridge, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models using three different descriptors representing the defect syste...

items.title: Thermoelectric properties of metal-semiconductor percolation composites
items.abstract: We analyze the thermoelectric response of composite materials comprising homogeneous semiconductor hosts with randomly distributed metallic inclusions. We demonstrate that the properties of such materials are strongly affected by the percolation transition (with background conductivity). We show that in the vicinity of the percolation threshold, the power factor and the thermoelectric figure of merit strongly depend on both the concentration and arrangement of inclusions. Finally, we identify promising regimes for enhancing the power factor in realistic composites.

items.title: Density-gradient effect in high-harmonic generation in gases
items.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gaseous targets is the most widespread method to produce coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulses with sub-femtosecond duration. However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light--matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale ima...

items.title: Optical Voltage Profiling of 2D Semiconductors via Proximal Exciton Sensing
items.abstract: High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. We introduce optical voltage profiling, a noninvasive wide-field technique that replaces local voltage probes with a proximal monolayer MoSe$_2$ exciton sensor. Isolated by thin hexagonal boron nitride, this sensor converts the target's local voltage into spatially resolved modulations of exciton reflectance. Through pixel-wise in situ calibration, these signals yield quantitative two-dimensional voltage maps of an actively biased semiconductor device. Using this method, we demonstrate the carrier-density-driven metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe$_2$ and obtain channel resistances of a few k$Ω$ despite M$Ω$-scale two-terminal resistances in the metallic region. items.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparenc...

items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. items.title: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor spin qubits have progressed from few-qubit demonstrations toward larger-scale devices fabricated in increasingly reproducible academic and industrial processes. This progress marks an inflection point: the central challenge is no longer to demonstrate high-fidelity operation in carefully tuned devices but to discover, verify, and maintain stable operating conditions reliably across many interdependent controls, varied device geometries, and disparate material platforms. In this Perspective, we frame spin-qubit operation as a modular automation problem. We decompose the workflow into five modules: bootstrapping from minimal prior information, configuration tuning, virtualization of physical gates into effective control axes, qubit-level tuning, and an operation layer with drift-aware maintenance.
